newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis again leads Swiss shares to record close.
newsitem.headline: Novartis again leads Swiss shares to record close.

text.p: Swiss shares jumped two percent on Thursday, driven by massive gains in index-heavyweight Novartis and derivatives-linked buying. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended above 5,500 points for the first time.
Novartis registered stock shot up 73 francs to 2,275 on a flurry of derivatives issues, analyst recommendations and this week's successful reseach presentation, dealers said.
"The bull run in Novartis triggered an actual buying spree," one dealer said. He added prospects for the market continued to be good. "There is no alternative to shares," he noted.
The SMI ended up 105.3 points, or 1.95 percent, at 5.510.3.
The index touched an all-time high at 5,529.8.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 59.79 points, or 1.74 percent, to 3,489.88.
Bourse volume reached a robust 3.58 billion Swiss francs.
"There were a few exaggerations, but you just cannot move against the tide," one trader noted.
Another dealer pointed out trade was heavily influenced by derivatives-linked transactions. "After Friday's expiry on Soffex, we may find out whether we need some time to relax," he said.
Other high-profile stocks such as Roche, UBS and Nestle posted gains of between one and two percent. Including Novartis, these four stocks make up about two-thirds of the SMI.

Shares of Credit Suisse Group stood out among major financials. The stock, which on Wednesday ended a recent period of decline, climbed 4.75 francs to 193.75. Dealers said old merger and spin-off speculation was revived.

Alusuisse was up 20 francs to 1,480, spurred by rumours ahead of the July 4 press conference. Dealers said there were hopes for a change in Alusuisse's strategy, although new CEO Sergio Marchionne earlier said he would stick to it.
